correction.text: Cliopatria's 110 shape without Margiana (Merv) and Sakastan, which Mithridates II holds again; held to -101

keyframe_overrides.why: The 110 shape gives the Saka Sistan and Margiana (the dossier's event 2, 'no page dates this'), but the Mithridates II page has 'Sometime between 124 and 115 BC, Mithridates II sent an army led by a general of the House of Suren', 'Sakastan was incorporated back into the Parthian realm', and coins struck at 'Marw in Margiana'. The Sakastan page's c. 100 BC (the dossier's reading) does not fit that page; the two cannot both be right and the opened page dates it before 115. Margiana (294 cells) and Sistan (256 cells) are cut; the keyframe also gets its 'to' of -101 that its own note states ('held to -101'; Cliopatria's row runs to -92 and would overlap indo-scythians_-91 from -100).

keyframe_overrides.why: New keyframe -135..-127: the dossier's ledger 8 ('split dongyue', 135) hands the whole kingdom to a counterpart that has no dossier, so Fujian, east Guangdong and south Zhejiang (680 cells) fall to nobody for nine years while minyue_-170 (checked only in -170) is meant to hold to -127 ('the page names no land for either king'). The Nanyue page has Minyue alive in 135 ('Minyue once again submitted to the Han dynasty, making itself and Nanyue equals once more') and the dossier's later keyframes carry the same shape from -126. The shape of minyue_-170 is repeated from -135.

The Indo-Scythian shape of -144 (Oxus country) overlaps Margiana by 291 cells; Parthia holds Merv.

region.text: Margiana, Sakastan and the middle Amu Darya, the land Mithridates II took back

rulings.why: Mithridates II page: 'Sometime between 124 and 115 BC, Mithridates II sent an army led by a general of the House of Suren' and 'Sakastan was incorporated back into the Parthian realm'; he 'reconquered western Bactria from the Scythians' and struck coins at 'Marw in Margiana'. By -110 these lands are Parthian; the Indo-Scythian shape of -110 overlaps them by 1,134 cells.
